messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Elevated packet loss (10-25%) and DNS resolution errors observed for CDN POP eu-central-1-edge-2. Potential impact to EU users. Thread id: 1752345678

 tom (oncall-sre): Noted. Seeing increased 5xx and socket timeouts for EU region. Traces show DNS failures and long DNS lookup latencies (~500-1200ms).

 nina (netops): I'm seeing intermittent NXDOMAIN responses from our secondary resolver for that POP. Upstream DNS provider reported a config push ~5m ago. 

 rachel (eng-runtime): Are origins responsive? Our origin health checks look green; edge nodes are failing to resolve namespaces for some routes leading to fallback failures. Streaming is impacted (clients report reconnections).

 deploy-bot: No CDN config deploys in last 30m.

 nina (netops): Running dig against edge-resolver: 
```
; <<>> DiG 9.11.3 <<>> api.us-eu.redwood.ai @10.20.30.40
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NXDOMAIN, id: 12345
;; flags: qr rd ra; QUERY: 1, ANSWER: 0
```

 nina (netops): Looks like our delegations lost a zone record on that provider's POP cluster. Im opening a ticket with them now (UP-99999).

 tom (oncall-sre): Immediate mitigation options: 1) Flip CDN POP to prefer eu-central-1-edge-1/edge-3 via traffic steering, 2) Add local resolver fallback to our internal DNS cache on the POP, 3) Emergency DNS entry injection at our edge for critical hostnames. Thoughts?

 rachel (eng-runtime): 1 and 2 are safest. We should avoid manual DNS injection unless necessary. If we steer traffic off the affected POP, will clients route seamlessly?

 nina (netops): Yes, we can update traffic steering for that POP to deprioritize it. Doing a gradual drain to avoid cache stampede. Also provisioning a local resolver patch on eu-central-1-edge-2 to use internal cache only. Applying now.

 tom (oncall-sre): Please also increase origin retry/backoff for short requests to reduce surface errors during cutover.

 rachel (eng-runtime): Patch: 
```
PATCH /infra/cdn/steering
pop.eu-central-1-edge-2.weight = 0.2
pop.eu-central-1-edge-1.weight = 0.5
pop.eu-central-1-edge-3.weight = 0.3
streaming.retries = 4
streaming.backoff = 1500ms
```

 ops-bot: CDN steering change applied. Health check window extended by 5m.

 nina (netops): Provider responded: they pushed a bad zonefile to a subset of their edge resolvers; engineering rollback initiated but some nodes still reflect bad state. Ticket UP-99999 opened.

 jorge (support): We have multiple EU customers reporting generation timeouts and reconnects. Im sending the standard status update: "We are mitigating an EU edge DNS issue by rerouting traffic to adjacent POPs; streaming retries increased. We'll post updates every 30 minutes." Add any specifics?

 tom (oncall-sre): Include affected POP id (eu-central-1-edge-2), provider ticket UP-99999, and note that origin health checks remain green so data integrity unaffected.

 rachel (eng-runtime): Observed a brief increase in origin load after reroute start (~12% CPU bump on EU origin pool) due to cache miss surge; we applied a conservative cache ttl bump and jitter to cold fills.

 ops-bot: Cache TTL modified for large responses: default_ttl = 45s, max_stale = 5s, jitter = true.

 tom (oncall-sre): Monitoring metrics: DNS error rate down from 18% to ~3% after steering; overall 5xxs reduced by 65%. Streaming success rate improving but still below baseline.

 nina (netops): Provider reports majority of their nodes recovered, but eu-central-1-edge-2 resolver cluster still shows anomalous responses. They suggest a full cache flush on their side.

 jorge (support): I've posted a customer-facing note and attached the incident link: status.redwood.ai/incidents/1752345678. Customers asking about ETA; what's reasonable?

 nina (netops): If provider finishes rollback and cache flush, should be fixed in ~15-30m. If not, we keep steering and schedule maintenance for that POP.

 tom (oncall-sre): Handoff plan: I'll be on watch for the next 20m. If metrics are stable for 15m, we'll consider re-weighting back. Leave emergency DNS injection as last resort.

 deploy-bot: No deploys scheduled to CDN control plane in next 60m.

 rachel (eng-runtime): Noting for postmortem: we saw a mid-cutover cache stampede pattern despite jitter; add runbook step to rate-limit cold-origin fetches during traffic shift.

 ops-bot: Incident state: MITIGATED -> monitoring. Severity set to SEV2. Next automated update in 20 minutes.

 tom (oncall-sre): 20m check: metrics stable. Provider confirms cache flush completed on 6/6 nodes but 2 nodes still regenerating. I'm going to slowly restore weights to 0.4/0.35/0.25 for edge-1/edge-2/edge-3 and watch for DNS errors.

 nina (netops): Rolling weight update applied. Watching for err spikes.

 jorge (support): Updating customers: were seeing improvements; continuing to monitor; ETA contingent on provider work.

 tom (oncall-sre): 40m mark: error rate returned to baseline, DNS lookups stable for all POPs. Re-enabling full traffic to eu-central-1-edge-2.

 nina (netops): Confirmed. Provider closed UP-99999 with root cause: bad zonefile push. Theyre adding additional k/v checks pre-push.

 incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: Resolved to stable. Final severity: SEV2 (regional DNS outage at CDN provider).

 rachel (eng-runtime): Actions for postmortem: 1) add automated per-pop DNS health checks (per-peer NXDOMAIN threshold), 2) runbook for traffic steering + cache ramp, 3) implement local resolver fallback by default for POPs, 4) consider automated provider failover if DNS errors exceed X% for Y minutes.

 tom (oncall-sre): I'll write the postmortem and link here in ~3 hours. Also creating follow-ups: DNSTM-12 (per-pop DNS checks), CDN-ROUT-7 (auto-steering thresholds), RUNBOOK-POP-OUTAGE.

 jorge (support): I'll close customer loops once postmortem is available.

 incident-bot: Reminder: attach postmortem doc here when available and label with SEV2.
